Chapter 7. Sustaining Motivation: Keeping the Fire Alive.
You know that special kind of energy you feel when you start something new? Maybe it's the first day of the season, or the launch of a big project. Everything just seems possible, and your motivation is sky-high. But, as the days roll by, and the routine starts to settle in, that spark can begin to fade a little, can't it? The real challenge isn’t just getting motivated—it’s holding onto that motivation, especially when progress feels slow or you run into a few setbacks.
Let me share a story. There was this team that started off strong. They were pumped, ready to take on anything. But as time went on, practices started to feel... well, a bit monotonous. The excitement that used to fill the room faded, replaced by a sense of obligation. Players were still showing up, but you could tell—their hearts just weren’t in it.
The coach saw what was happening and decided it was time for a change. Instead of another regular strategy session, he asked everyone to share what inspired them. What brought them to the game? Why did they love to compete? Why did they want to be a part of this team?
The answers? They were as different as the players themselves. Some talked about the rush of competition, others about the friendships they’d made, and a few opened up about wanting to prove something to themselves. Hearing each other’s stories reminded the whole team why they started in the first place.
Inspired by that, the coach encouraged everyone to set their own personal goals, alongside the team’s goals. He wanted them to find meaning in the daily grind, not just in chasing the big wins.
Here’s something to pay attention to—motivation isn’t something you can just force. It has to be cared for, day after day, in those small, meaningful moments of connection and purpose. The most motivated teams? They’re the ones who find ways to celebrate every bit of progress, who recognize each other’s effort, and who never lose sight of the bigger picture.
They also know when to make time for fun, for rest, and for reflecting on how far they’ve come. Because, let’s be honest, burnout is the real enemy of lasting success.
Most people think motivation is all about willpower—just push through, no matter what. But if you look at the teams that really last, they’re the ones who know how to recharge, reconnect with their purpose, and have each other’s backs through all the ups and downs. They get that motivation comes and goes—and that it’s totally normal to have off days, as long as you keep coming back to what truly matters.
So, what’s the invisible game in these moments? It’s about finding meaning in the journey, not just chasing after the destination. The teams that keep their fire alive are the ones who stay connected—to their goals, to each other, and to the reasons they fell in love with the game in the first place.
